text:
alex: seeing a sudden surge of 500/503s hitting hosted inference around 09:23 UTC, looks like upstream inference runner(s) are crashing and being restarted repeatedly. customers A & B reported timeouts. seeing GPU OOM + segfault pattern in the logs. any oncall?
ops-bot: alert: infer-runner-eviction-surge cluster=hosted-us-east-2, affected=8 pods, symptom=503s, severity=high
maria: assigning oncall. i'm on it — looking at logs + metrics. alex, can you paste the last few crash logs and coredump summary?
alex: pasting snippet from /var/log/infer-runner.log and dmesg:```
[2026-03-17T09:22:41Z] runner: Alloc failed: requested 3.2GB, available 1.1GB -> GPU OOM
[2026-03-17T09:22:41Z] runner: segfault at 0 ip 0x7f9a... stack trace: nvmlDeviceReset called -> SIGSEGV
[2026-03-17T09:22:42Z] kubelet: Container killed, reason=OOMKilled
--- coredump saved to /var/crash/runner.1234.core
```
sam: hmm looks like a burst of high-context requests triggered a prefetch+batch resize path that allocs too much memory. recent commit that adjusted batch growth might regress memory accounting. any recent deploys to the runtime pool?
alex: nope no deploys in last 2 hrs, but we did flip a routing policy for a customer earlier which increased QPS to that pool.
maria: immediate mitigation steps: 1) enable fallback routing to redirect new requests away from the affected pool, 2) set pool autoscale to +2 GPUs, 3) disable KV prefetch feature flag for hosted-us-east-2. doing 1 now.
maria: `curl -X POST https://console.internal/api/pools/fallback -d '{"pool":"hosted-us-east-2","enable":true}'` -> success :white_check_mark:
rebecca: support: customers A (ticket #2371) and B (#2378) are being impacted, both see 503s and timeouts on key endpoints. I've posted an interim update to both. pls ping me when we have ETA for fix and when rollback/mitigation complete.
sam: can someone grab the core and run `gdb --batch -ex 'bt full' -ex quit runner.1234.core` and post the backtrace? also check `nvidia-smi --query-gpu=memory.free,memory.used --format=csv` history for the node.
alex: attaching gdb bt output (trimmed):```
#0  0x00007f9a.. in gpu_kernel()
#1  0x00007f8b.. in kv_prefetch()
#2  0x0000555f.. in handle_request()
#3  0x0000555f.. in main_loop()
```
looks like kv_prefetch() touching an already-freed buffer when mixed with aggressive batch growth.
maria: rolling restart of affected pool to pick up immediate config change. starting restart sequence now, doing 4 at a time to avoid coldstart spike.
maria: also toggled `REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=false` on the pool config.
ops-bot: action: fallback routing enabled for hosted-us-east-2 (policy id 0x7a), pool scale +2, feature-flag REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=false
rebecca: customer update sent: "we've routed traffic away from the impacted servers, temporary mitigations are in place, and engineering is investigating root cause. we'll follow up with a timeline."
alex: repro steps for engineering to reproduce locally:
1) checkout branch `perf/batch-dynamic`
2) run `make docker-build && docker run --gpus all -e REDWOOD_KV_PREFETCH=1 runner:test`
3) run load test: `wrk -t12 -c500 -d60s --script scripts/large-context.lua http://localhost:8080`
4) observe memory growth and OOMs when batch resize triggers.
sam: thanks. short-term patch options: limit max_batch_growth to 1.5x, add an allocation guard in kv_prefetch, or skip prefetch when free GPU memory < 2GB. which do we prefer for a quick hotfix?
maria: prefer toggle + config limit change first (safer). will push pool config change to cap batch growth to 1.25x and enable guard alerting. applying now.
maria: patch applied to pool config: `max_batch_growth=1.25`, alert rule added for GPU free < 1.5GB.
ops-bot: rollout: pool config updated, restart rolling (4/24 done).
alex: after first wave of restarts we see error rate drop from 18% -> 3% for this pool. customers still see some spikes but much improved.
rebecca: logging final customer note and will keep monitoring. will close ticket when stable for 30m.
sam: next steps for engineering: 1) reproduce and write regression test, 2) revert unguarded batch-growth commit or add safety checks, 3) postmortem with timeline + code change. I'll own the regression test.
maria: agreed. creating incident runbook entry and scheduling postmortem doc.
rebecca: thanks everyone — great coordinated response. :thumbsup:
